question: What is the term for a group of similar cells working together?
explanation: A tissue is defined as a collection of similar cells that work together to perform a specific function in the body. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h1)

question: How do tissues and organs relate to each other structurally?

options.D: Organs break down into single tissues

explanation: Different types of tissues group together to build organs, which then carry out major body activities. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h1)

question: Which primary tissue type is responsible for body movement?
explanation: Muscle tissue contains contractile cells that shorten to produce movement of the skeleton and internal organs. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four primary tissue types?
explanation: Skeletal tissue is a specific subtype of muscle tissue, not one of the four primary tissue categories. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h2)

question: Why do epithelial tissues rely on underlying connective tissues for survival?
explanation: Because epithelial tissues do not contain blood vessels, they must absorb nutrients via diffusion from the vascularized connective tissue beneath them. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h3)

question: What is the main role of the extracellular matrix in connective tissue?
explanation: The extracellular matrix provides structural strength, elasticity, and physical anchorage for surrounding cells and organs. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h3)

question: Which membrane type lines closed cavities inside the ventral body cavity?
explanation: Serous membranes line closed internal body cavities, such as the pleural and peritoneal cavities, reducing friction with watery fluid. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h4)

question: A patient with knee joint inflammation has excess fluid buildup in which specific membrane?
explanation: Synovial membranes line joint cavities and produce synovial fluid, which can accumulate during joint inflammation or injury. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h4)

question: What is the primary difference between tissue regeneration and fibrosis?

options.A: Regeneration restores original function, while fibrosis creates scar tissue
options.B: Fibrosis happens rapidly, while regeneration takes many years
options.C: Fibrosis occurs only in the skin, while regeneration occurs in bones
options.D: Regeneration produces collagen, while fibrosis produces epithelial cells

explanation: Regeneration replaces lost cells with functional tissue of the same type, whereas fibrosis lays down fibrous scar tissue without original function. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h5)

question: Why does damage to cardiac muscle tissue often result in permanent functional impairment?

options.A: Blood vessels cannot reach damaged heart muscle
options.B: Heart muscle cells divide too rapidly to form scars
options.C: Cardiac muscle cells have poor regenerative capacity
options.D: Cardiac tissue lacks any extracellular matrix proteins

explanation: Cardiac muscle cells do not readily divide, so the heart heals damaged areas through fibrous scar formation rather than regeneration. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h5)

question: Why does a nurse regularly reposition a bedridden patient to protect tissue health?

options.A: To increase the production of synovial fluid in joint cavities
options.B: To convert fibrous scar tissue back into epithelial tissue
options.C: To prevent pressure-induced ischemia in skin and underlying tissues
options.D: To stimulate rapid regeneration of cardiac muscle cells

explanation: Sustained body weight cuts off blood flow to cutaneous and subcutaneous tissues, causing ischemia and pressure ulcers if not relieved. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h6)

question: What is a major systemic risk when extensive areas of the cutaneous membrane are destroyed by burns?

options.A: Excessive accumulation of synovial joint fluid
options.B: Immediate regeneration of all damaged layers
options.C: Severe fluid loss and increased infection risk
options.D: Rapid overproduction of nervous tissue cells

explanation: The cutaneous membrane acts as a barrier against fluid evaporation and microbial invasion; its destruction leads to dehydration and sepsis. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h6)
